patch.objective: Evaluating external business-environment changes (regulatory, technological, geopolitical, market) and their impact on project scope or backlog
secondaryObjectives: Aligning and managing stakeholder expectations: categorizing stakeholders, facilitating alignment discussions, and monitoring internal/external customer satisfaction

sources.cite: PMI, Project Management Professional (PMP) Examination Content Outline, July 2026 Update: People 33%, Process 41%, Business Environment 26%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of a copy of PMI's PDF hosted by a training provider (the course seed cites PMI's own copy). Relevant text: Domain II Task 3 'Help ensure value-based delivery' ('Prioritize work based on value and stakeholder feedback'; 'Assess opportunities to deliver value incrementally'); Task 8 'Plan and manage schedule' ('Baseline a project schedule'; 'Analyze schedule variation'); Domain III Task 3 'Manage and control changes' ('Execute the change control process'); Task 4 'Remove impediments and manage issues' ('Evaluate the impact of impediments'; 'Recognize when a risk becomes an issue'); Task 5 'Plan and manage risk'; Task 8 'Evaluate external business environment changes' ('Assess and prioritize the impact on project scope/backlog based on changes in the external business environment'). The objective wording here is the course seed's.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). The Sprint: 'No changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal'; 'Quality does not decrease'; 'Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned'. 'A Sprint could be cancelled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete. Only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel the Sprint.'

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Sprint Backlog: 'If the work turns out to be different than they expected, they collaborate with the Product Owner to negotiate the scope of the Sprint Backlog within the Sprint without affecting the Sprint Goal.' Sprints are fixed length, one month or less.

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Product Owner: 'The Product Owner may represent the needs of many stakeholders in the Product Backlog. Those wanting to change the Product Backlog can do so by trying to convince the Product Owner.'

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Definition of Done: an item that does not meet it 'cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review'; it returns to the Product Backlog.
